item.title: A Pain Patch That Pricks First | Episode 310
item.description:
In one sentence: TEAM is an experimental microneedle electrotherapy patch that uses conductive microneedles to cross the skin’s high-resistance outer layer and deliver more controlled electrical stimulation—without putting pain medication in the needles.

Key points

  • The microneedles are conductive contacts, not drug-delivery tubes.
  • A conductive hydrogel provides a parallel current path and helps distribute current across the skin surface.
  • A constant-current circuit compensates for changes in skin impedance; it does not choose treatment settings or diagnose pain.
  • The evidence includes animal studies and quantitative sensory testing in ten healthy volunteers, not long-term clinical proof in patients with chronic pain.
  • Automatic activation used threshold rules based on optical pulse signals; heart rate and heart-rate variability are not pain-specific.

This episode explains what TEAM changes in the hardware, what the experiments actually show, and why “closed loop” does not mean that a patch can understand your pain.
